versions.name: RXV2-0.9.222-fly-menu
versions.notes: Radios-off mode gets a proper front door: from the RF-only screen you can now return to the menu WITHOUT re-enabling the radios, and while they're off the Fly-now slot becomes a big green 'Re-enable WiFi & Bluetooth' button. The Bluetooth badge hides while the radios are off (the receiver is only whispering down one kept link). Also fixes the kept Bluetooth link going mute after fly-arm — the return buttons now genuinely work. Installing this also updates the web pages.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.221-fly-ui
versions.notes: Fly-screen polish: the 'turns off WiFi & Bluetooth' note sits neatly under 'Fly now' instead of squashed beside it, and the return button on the RF-only screen now says 'Turn WiFi & Bluetooth back ON' in big friendly letters - it's rather important, after all. Installing this also updates the web pages.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.220-fly-ble
versions.notes: Fly now enters the Bluetooth era: the button says what it does (turns off WiFi AND Bluetooth), every screen names both radios, and when you're connected by Bluetooth the 'RF-only' screen keeps ONE quiet link alive (no advertising) so it can offer a Return-to-menu button - tap it and the receiver reboots with both radios back, the app reconnecting by itself. Close the app instead and that last link goes silent for interference-free flying. Also: firmware installs over Bluetooth now confirm before rebooting. Installing this also updates the web pages.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.219-update-test
versions.notes: No functional change - identical to 0.9.218 apart from the version number. Released to prove the new persistent update-offer works end to end (connect over Bluetooth, see the offer appear, tap to install).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.218-update-check
versions.notes: The 'Update available' offer no longer gets missed when you connect quickly after powering the receiver. The home page used to check for new firmware exactly once - if the receiver's WiFi was still coming up at that moment (typical in the first seconds after power-on) the check answered 'offline' and the offer silently never appeared, though a later connection (or another phone) would see it. The page now keeps quietly re-checking for a couple of minutes until the receiver is online, so the offer pops up as soon as it can be known. Installing this also updates the web pages; your Rotorflight backups are preserved.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.217-ble-name
versions.notes: ANDROID! The receiver now works with the new RXV2 Android app as well as the iPhone app. Bluetooth is far more dependable on every phone: replies are sent in chunks every device can swallow (some Androids quietly drop oversized packets even after promising a big one), sized to the connection's true negotiated limit, with a larger buffer pool so a whole page queues at once. Also fixes the Bluetooth scan NAME - the receiver now correctly advertises your model's name (e.g. 'BenchTest') instead of appearing nameless or as a stale cached name; a subtle ordering bug meant the name never fitted into the advertisement. Installing this also updates the web pages; your Rotorflight backups are preserved.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.212-ble-config
versions.notes: BLUETOOTH! Configure the receiver from the new RXV2 iPhone app over Bluetooth LE - no hotspot-joining dance, faster and more dependable than WiFi, and perfect at the field (the WiFi web setup is unchanged for everyone else). The View-channels page is now silky: the receiver PUSHES channel data continuously over Bluetooth, bars and the 3D helicopter animate smoothly through radio hiccups, and the ARMED indicator is live. Home page shows one pill per transceiver slot - green 'receiving' follows whichever radio carries your transmitter right now. Also: WiFi+Bluetooth coexistence boot-loop cured, wrapped-banner layout fixed, and every help screen explains the ways to connect. Installing this also updates the web pages; your Rotorflight backups are preserved.
